spans.text: False positives cost -3 points each — sloppy reports destroy your net value
spans.note: The prompt strongly emphasizes truthfulness and information integrity. It penalizes false positives (-3 points each), requires verification of claims against documentation, mandates honest reporting of coverage, and instructs the agent to skip findings it cannot verify. The prompt explicitly states 'If you haven't read it, skip it' and 'If it requires impossible preconditions, skip it,' and requires noting when documentation could not be verified.

spans.text: After main analysis, check each CRITICAL/HIGH file for: hardcoded secrets, JWT/session without expiry, weak crypto (MD5/SHA1 for passwords), unvalidated request body, no Content-Type/size limits, unvalidated numeric inputs, non-expiring tokens, user enumeration via error messages, sensitive fields in responses, exposed stack traces, missing rate limiting on auth, missing CSRF, open redirects.
spans.note: The prompt actively instructs the agent to detect and report security vulnerabilities related to data protection, including hardcoded secrets, sensitive data exposure, and credential leaks. It includes specific checks for hardcoded credentials (CWE-798) and sensitive data exposure (CWE-200) in its security checklist and CWE reference table.

spans.text: Only analyze files listed in your assignment. Cross-references to outside files: note in UNTRACED CROSS-REFS but don't investigate.
spans.note: The prompt demonstrates strong tool/action safety principles. It enforces strict scope rules (only analyze assigned files), uses a read-only analysis approach (Read tool, Glob tool), and does not instruct the agent to execute any code. The agent writes output to a specific file path and follows a structured, non-destructive workflow. It also actively detects security vulnerabilities like injection, SSRF, and path traversal.
